title: Build a per-district token budget
prompt:
Your Claude-powered tutor is sold to school districts, and each district's contract includes a daily token allowance. One district's busy morning must not spend another district's budget, and many tutoring calls run at the same time, so you can't wait until a call finishes to count it.

The pattern: reserve an estimate before calling the model (input tokens + max_tokens), then settle with the real number from the API's usage when the call finishes, or release if it failed. Implement class TokenBudget:

  • new TokenBudget({ dailyLimits, defaultLimit, clock }). Budgets are per district per UTC day: Math.floor(clock.now() / DAY_MS).
  • remaining(tenant): limit minus settled usage minus open reservations, today; never below 0.
  • reserve(tenant, estimatedTokens): if it fits, hold it and return { ok: true, id } (ids 'r1', 'r2', ...). Otherwise return { ok: false, reason: 'over_budget', remaining } and hold nothing.
  • settle(id, actualTokens): replace the estimate with the actual usage (actual can be lower or higher). release(id): give it all back. Both are no-ops for unknown or already finished ids.
budget.reserve('lincoln', 4000);   // { ok: true, id: 'r1' }   remaining 6000
budget.settle('r1', 1500);          //                         remaining 8500

tests.name: reserve holds tokens; settle swaps the estimate for actual usage
in-flight reservations count: concurrent calls cannot overspend
districts are isolated; unknown districts get the default limit
actual usage above the estimate is charged; remaining floors at 0
release returns everything; settle and release are idempotent
budget resets at UTC midnight (injected clock)

hints: Keep a map keyed by tenant + '|' + day holding { used, reserved }, and a second map from reservation id to { key, tokens }. The day key makes midnight resets free: a new day is simply a new, empty bucket.

reserve compares the estimate with remaining(tenant) before adding to reserved. settle looks up the reservation, deletes it (that is what makes a second call a no-op), subtracts its tokens from reserved and adds the actual tokens to used.
release(id) is just settle(id, 0). Store the bucket key on the reservation so a call that started at 23:59 settles against the day it was reserved on.
explain:
This is the reserve-then-settle (or "authorize then capture") pattern that card payments use, applied to LLM spend. In production the counters live in Redis (an atomic Lua script or INCRBY with a check) or in Postgres rows, not in one process's memory, because many API servers share the budget. You would usually also have a per-district request-rate limit (token bucket) on top, and alert at 80% of budget so the district hears from you before students hit a wall.

Say it in the interview: "Anthropic rate limits and bills my organization, not my customers, so fairness and cost control per tenant are my job. Before each call I reserve input tokens plus max_tokens against the district's budget, then settle with the actual usage from the response. Reservations stop concurrent requests from overspending, and the budget is checked before we spend a cent."
